messages:
jamie: heads up — canary rollout for model v2.3.0 started ~10m ago, staging flags show +25% p50 gen latency on short prompts. Not consistent across instances tho.
alex: stop the rollout? :thinking:
jamie: I already hit the 'pause rollout' button in console, but canary is ~30% through. we should block further shards until we triage.
dev-bot: CI perf-checker: job perf/regression detected on pr #1894 — p50 increase 23% (baseline: 48ms -> current: 59ms). Full log: https://ci.internal/runs/98765
sara: thanks. which commits shipped with v2.3.0? my vague memory: tokenizer normalization tweak + kernel selection fallback refactor + batch heuristic tweak.
toni: putting up a quick profile of a failed trace — looks like tokenization output lengths shifted (avg tokens per input +12%) which is causing more KV flushes and preventing kernel reuse. snippet:
```
/* sample perf stack (short prompt) */
conv_tokenize: 8.2ms
kv_cache_lookup: 1.1ms
kernel_select: 4.9ms -> chosen: fallback_kernel_fp16_slow
compute_attention: 42.3ms
total: 59.5ms
```
previously total ~48ms with `fast_kernel_int8` chosen.
leo: that matches what i saw locally. tokenizer normalization change (PR 1878) added NFC normalization for some punctuation. it bumps token counts for a small slice of inputs, but seems to cascade: different seq len -> different kernel heuristic -> worse perf.
alex: ok. action items: 1) bisect between PR 1878 (tokenizer) and PR 1902 (kernel fallback) — either could be the trigger 2) revert candidate if bisect confirms 3) add guard in rollout to compare token length distribution before/after.
jamie: starting bisect now. running canary traces pinned to the same seed inputs to reproduce. will post short results.
sara: also raise a quick CI job to run sampled tokenizers on the onboarding checkpoint. maybe the new model checkpoint (ckpt-2026-04) has slightly different whitespace canonicalization, which + tokenizer change = worst-case.
toni: microbench script (run locally):
```
python perf/check_tokenizer.py --model ckpt-2026-04 --samples 5000 --dump-hist
# expect mean_len ~ 18.7
```
leo: running that now, will paste hist.
leo: hist result: mean_len before=18.4, after=20.6; p90 jump from 27 -> 33. that's significant for kernel selection thresholds.
dev-bot: perf-bisect: bisect run started between commits 1840..1905. ETA ~12m.
jamie: if bisect points to tokenizer PR, i propose temporary revert of 1878 and roll forward kernel fallback changes separately. we can't ship both until we add kernel heuristic that is length-aware for the pancake-fallback.
alex: agreed. also add a CI perf test that runs tokenizer distribution diff and fails if mean_len delta > 5% for onboarding builds.
sara: filing a quick ticket for the guard and linking to the bisect + canary traces. ticket #INF-872.
jamie: update: bisect narrowed it to PR 1878 (tokenizer normalization). reverting now in staging. patch: `git revert --no-commit 1878` then re-run canary.
toni: once revert is applied, please run the microbench script again so we can confirm kernel selection returns to baseline.
jamie: revert applied, canary restarted. initial p50 after revert ~49ms (within noise). reverting blocked rollout resumed to full. marking as rollback-perf.
leo: leaving a note: we still need to harden kernel selection so small length shifts don't force the slow fallback — follow-up work item in INF-872.
jamie: closing loop here — root cause: tokenizer config drift (normalization) increased token counts -> changed kernel selection heuristics -> KV cache miss pattern and higher compute. revert + CI guard deployed. thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
